newsitem.title: UK: UK prompt natural gas dips, fourth quarter holds.
newsitem.headline: UK prompt natural gas dips, fourth quarter holds.

text.p: The U.K. natural gas spot market eased slightly on the prompt side on Friday but otherwise trade held within ranges set in recent days.
Activity was focused almost exclusively in the fourth quarter, in line with the IPE screen.
The prompt market was slightly weaker, dipping back below the key nine pence a therm level. Weekend gas traded at 8.90 and 8.95 pence a therm while September slipped to trade at 8.95 pence.
October was heavily traded, with one major shipper dominating proceedings.
The shipper sold early on at a soft 10.775 to reel in a string of offers at 10.80, at which price the buyer bought nearly 500,000 therms per day.
But the contango into the winter months held more or less steady, with November traded at 12.85 pence a therm and the first quarter ending steady after being talked higher in early discussion.
Next summer was thinly traded and held steady at 10.775 pence.
Trade on the IPE screen slowed after brisk volumes were traded on Thursday which helped open interest climb to over 6,000 lots.
On Friday open interest reached 6,210 lots, equivalent to nearly 190 million therms, or nearly double the daily level of gas production in the U.K.
"It is clear that the natural gas futures contract is becoming increasingly important to the industry," said Richard Ward, head of business development at the IPE said in a statement.
